**Date:** {{< meta display-date >}}  
**From:** {{< meta from-address >}}  
**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

It is in an appendix to collected editions of [Mrs.

Hemans](../persons.html#1936)’ life and works, where she had made notes of subjects from history suitable to write poems upon, unluckily without saying where they came from. I have watched for this story for years . . . I will write to the friend who owns the copy of Mrs Hemans from which I took it.[^1]

[^1]: [Alfred Tennyson](../persons.html#1874) had asked [Warburton](../persons.html#1466) (later a canon of Winchester but at that date an inspector of schools) to find out from CMY the source of the story, ‘Odin’s Sacrifice’, in the [Book of Golden Deeds](../books.html#51).

On 6 June 1865, he quoted this extract from one of two letters he had received from her.

Tennyson used the story in his poem \'The Victim\'.
